title: How do you build a competency framework?
seoTitle: How to build a competency framework
description: An eight step method for building a competency framework: scope, structure, sources, drafting, proficiency levels, validation, role profiles and governance.
shortAnswer: A competency framework is built by fixing its purpose and scope, choosing a structure of domains, competencies, indicators and proficiency levels, gathering evidence of what competent work looks like, drafting competencies as observable statements, writing distinct proficiency levels, validating them with job holders and experts, assigning required levels to roles, and putting the framework under version control with a named owner and review cycle.
keyTakeaways: Decide what the framework will be used for (recruitment, training, assessment, regulatory evidence) before drafting anything. Purpose drives granularity.
Reuse authoritative sources where they exist: national occupational standards or units of competency, professional standards and regulator guidance.
Write each competency as observable performance, with behavioral indicators an assessor could actually check.
Proficiency levels should differ in autonomy, complexity and judgment, as national qualifications frameworks such as the AQF do, not just in adjectives like 'basic' and 'advanced'.
A framework without an owner, a version number and a review date decays within a year.

sections.heading: What does a competency framework contain?

blocks.text: A [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework) contains a set of competencies grouped into domains, a description of what each competency looks like in practice, proficiency levels that show how performance develops, and role profiles that state which level each role needs.

The definition of competence matters here. ISO 9000:2015 defines competence as the 'ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results', as quoted by the ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group ([ISO and IAF](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176/files/PDF%20APG%20New%20Disclaimer%2012-2023/ISO-TC%20176-TF_APG-Competence.pdf)). A framework built on that definition describes application and results, not just knowledge.

sections.heading: What are the steps to build a competency framework?

blocks.text: There are eight steps. The first two are decisions, steps three to six build the content, and the last two make it usable and keep it current.

items: **Fix purpose and scope.** Write down the uses the framework must support and the roles or job families it covers. A framework for regulatory evidence needs finer, assessable indicators than one used only for career conversations. Output: a one page charter naming the sponsor, the owner and the in scope roles.

**Choose the structure.** Decide the hierarchy (domain, competency, indicator), the number of proficiency levels, and the fields each competency record will hold. Output: a template for a single competency record.

**Gather evidence of competent performance.** Collect procedures, role descriptions, regulator guidance, incident and quality data, and existing standards. Where national occupational standards exist, use them. For example, Australia's national units of competency on training.gov.au already express workplace performance as elements and performance criteria; the Training Package Organizing Framework requires elements to 'describe demonstrable workplace outcomes' ([DEWR](https://www.dewr.gov.au/download/16680/training-package-organising-framework-effective-1-july-2025/39042/training-package-organising-framework/pdf)). Output: a source register listing every document used and its version.

**Run structured sessions with job holders and experts.** Use critical incident questions (describe a time this task went well, and a time it went badly) to surface what separates competent from non-competent performance. Output: raw task and behavior statements, tagged to sources.

**Draft competencies and indicators.** Cluster the statements into competencies, write each as an action verb plus object plus context, and write three to six indicators per competency. Remove overlaps so each behavior belongs to one competency only. Output: a draft competency catalog.

**Write proficiency levels.** Describe each level by changes in autonomy, complexity of situations handled, judgment and responsibility for others. National qualifications frameworks use a similar logic. For example, the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) describes application of knowledge and skills in terms of autonomy, judgment and responsibility across its ten levels ([AQF](https://www.aqf.edu.au/framework/aqf-levels)). Output: level descriptors for every competency.

**Validate.** Test the draft with a different group of job holders and managers from those who helped write it. Ask them to rate relevance and clarity, and to place real (anonymised) examples of work at a level. Where raters disagree, the wording is ambiguous. Output: a validation log with changes made.

**Build role profiles and govern.** Assign the required level of each competency to each role, publish the framework with a version number, and set a review cycle and triggers such as regulatory change. Output: role profiles and a governance record.

sections.heading: What does a finished competency entry look like?

blocks.text: A finished entry states the competency, its indicators and what distinguishes each level. The example below is illustrative: it is not drawn from any published framework, and an organization would ground the indicators in its own procedures and regulator guidance.

blocks.caption: Illustrative competency record: assessing unusual customer activity
head: Level
Descriptor
Sample indicator
rows: Foundation
Recognizes listed indicators of unusual activity in routine interactions and escalates using the set procedure, under supervision
Escalates a transaction showing a listed indicator within the required time
Practitioner
Assesses unusual activity across customer types and products, gathers relevant context and makes a documented escalation decision without supervision
Records the reasons for escalating or not escalating, with reference to the procedure
Expert
Handles complex and novel patterns, advises others, and identifies where procedures or indicators need to change
Proposes an indicator change supported by case analysis and has it approved

blocks.text: Notice that the levels differ by autonomy and complexity, and each indicator names something an assessor could observe or inspect. That property is what makes the framework usable for [competency assessment](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: Which existing standards can a competency framework reuse?

blocks.text: Reuse existing standards wherever they fit, because they have already been consulted on and are recognized by regulators and auditors.

items: **National occupational standards or units of competency** for vocational tasks, such as the units of competency described in step three, with their performance criteria, performance evidence and knowledge evidence.
**Professional or practice standards** issued by professional bodies or regulators, for example standards for financial advisers or clinicians.

**Regulator guidance** that states the knowledge and skills people in regulated roles are expected to have. Where a regulator publishes this, cite the specific guide and version in your source register.

**National skills classifications.** Where your country publishes a skills taxonomy or occupational classification, it can supply core competencies, specializt tasks and technology tools as a starting list. Check its currency and status before relying on it.

blocks.title: Check before you import
blocks.text: Imported statements often describe a whole occupation. Cut them down to what your roles actually do, and record the source and version for each imported item so it can be updated when the source changes.

Most frameworks fail because they are too abstract to assess or too large to maintain. A framework nobody can assess against becomes a poster; a framework with hundreds of competencies becomes shelfware.

items: Values dressed as competencies ('shows integrity') with no observable indicators.
Proficiency levels that differ only by adjectives.
No link to the [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) or assessment, so the framework never affects what people are trained on.
No owner and no review trigger, so it drifts away from current procedures.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry stores competencies, the concepts they depend on, their sources and their assessment points as linked records with version history. When a source changes, the affected competencies and the training built on them can be identified. See [framework intelligence](/platform/framework-intelligence).

faqs.q: How many competencies should a framework have?
faqs.a: Enough to cover the performance that matters and no more. Role specific frameworks often work with a small number of domains and a few competencies in each. If a role profile lists more competencies than a manager could discuss in a performance conversation, the framework is probably too granular for that purpose.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a competency and a skill?
faqs.a: A skill is a specific ability, such as using a system or calculating a figure. A competency combines knowledge, skills and behavior applied to achieve a result in a work context. The [competency framework vs skills framework](/compare/competency-framework-vs-skills-framework) comparison covers this in detail.

faqs.q: How many proficiency levels should a framework use?
faqs.a: Three to five is common. Fewer than three rarely distinguishes learners from experts; more than five is hard for assessors to apply consistently. Choose the smallest number whose descriptors raters can tell apart reliably in validation.

faqs.q: How often should a competency framework be reviewed?
faqs.a: Set a scheduled review, commonly annual, plus event triggers: a change in regulation, a new product or system, a restructure, or audit findings. Record each review, even when no change is made, so there is evidence the framework was checked.
